newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian cotton harvest will be 100,000 tonnes up.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian cotton harvest will be 100,000 tonnes up.

text.p: The Egyptian cotton harvest this year will be about 100,000 tonnes bigger than last year's and the country will be able to export at least 50,000 tonnes, Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said in remarks published on Tuesday.

Last year's harvest was 260,000 tonnes and an earlier estimate was that this year's would be about 350,000 tonnes, mainly because the area planted is larger. Exports last year were only 19,000 tonnes despite very high world prices.

Ganzouri confirmed private-sector reports that the state would let spinning companies import cotton from anywhere in the world provided it met disease control regulations. He was quoted by the government newspaper al-Akhbar.
The liberalised cotton import regime will free more of Egypt's high-value long-staple cotton for export.
In the past Egypt allowed cotton imports only from California and Arizona because of fears that cotton from other areas would bring in dangerous pests and diseases.
The cotton marketing year started on September 1 and the first Egyptian farmers are just beginning to harvest.

The state is guaranteeing them a minimum price of 500 pounds a qantar (50 kg), the equivalent of 133 centilibres (U.S. cents per lb). Private traders are worried they will not be able to match the state price, which is above current world levels. --Jonathan Wright +20 2 578 3290/1
